content:
Rehabilitation of Nuevo Laredo's Colector Ribereño Centro sewer collector is 94.01 percent complete, the municipal government reported, a project of 112,955,425 pesos aimed at improving the sanitary drainage system and reducing the risk of wastewater discharges into the Rio Grande.

The project, carried out through the municipal water utility COMAPA, replaces sanitary infrastructure about 80 years old in one of the city's oldest sectors, according to CML Noticias. The work includes rehabilitating the collector and replacing household drinking-water connections and sanitary discharges, with the goal of improving how the networks function and preventing leaks and structural failures.

So far, 1,263 linear meters of pipe have been installed in section 2 as part of the work to strengthen wastewater conveyance, the report said.

A key goal of the project is to lower the risk of wastewater reaching the Rio Grande, a natural resource shared by Mexico and the United States, according to the report. The project is funded with non-reimbursable money from the Border Environment Infrastructure Fund, with resources from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency administered through the North American Development Bank.

Sources:
